title: Hiyashi Chuka
subtitle: cold ramen noodle salad with toppings and sesame dressing
excerpt: Hiyashi chuka is a Japanese cold noodle dish of chilled ramen topped with colourful strips of egg, cucumber, and chicken in a sharp sesame and soy dressing. It is served only in summer and signals the season wherever it appears. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Hiyashi chuka was created in Japan in the 1930s as a summer alternative to hot ramen. The dish is so strongly seasonal that many restaurants only put it on the menu from June to August.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook and chill the noodles and chicken up to 4 hours ahead. Prepare toppings and dressing in advance. Assemble just before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: A sharp, savoury-sweet dressing for cold noodles made from rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and a small amount of sugar.
Thinly cooked Japanese omelette strips used as a topping for cold noodle dishes. The name means 'golden thread egg'.

content.text: Hiyashi chuka is dressed with a sharp
egg strips, sliced chicken, and cucumber arranged in neat sections across the noodles. The contrast of cold noodles and sharp dressing is what makes summer feel like summer. Serves 4.
Rinse the cooked ramen noodles very thoroughly under cold water. Any residual starch will make the noodles sticky and dull the dressing.

Cook the ramen noodles in boiling water according to the packet. Drain, rinse well under cold running water for 2 minutes rubbing to remove starch, then transfer to iced water. Drain again and refrigerate.
Poach the chicken breast in simmering water for 12 minutes until cooked through. Cool in the liquid, then shred into thin strips. Chill.

Make the kinshi tamago: heat a thin film of oil in a 26 cm frying pan over medium heat. Pour in a thin layer of beaten egg, just enough to coat the base. Cook for 1 minute until set. Slide out, roll loosely, and cut into thin strips. Repeat with remaining egg.
Whisk all the dressing ingredients together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.

Divide the cold noodles between 4 bowls. Arrange the chicken, egg strips, cucumber, spring onion, and bean sprouts in neat sections on top. Pour the dressing over each bowl and scatter with sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

attrs.symptom: Noodles are clumping in the bowl
attrs.cause: The noodles were not rinsed long enough or were left undressed for too long.
attrs.fix: Rinse noodles for a full 2 minutes and toss with a few drops of sesame oil if not serving immediately.
Add an extra teaspoon of mirin and taste again. The dressing should be tangy but not mouth-puckering.

attrs.symptom: Egg strips are tearing when rolled
attrs.cause: The omelette layer was too thin or overcooked.
attrs.fix: Use a slightly thicker egg layer and remove from heat while the top is still barely set.

content.text: Hiyashi chuka is one of Japan's clearest signals of summer. Ramen shops put a sign in the window when they start offering it. The dish was invented in the 1930s when a ramen restaurant in Sendai wanted something to serve in summer. It caught on immediately. The colourful toppings arranged in sections give it a visual orderliness that is very Japanese. Every component has its place.
